merger_name: Coles - supermarket site in Palmwoods, QLD
merger_description:
Coles Group Limited (**Coles**) is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that primarily operates:

* supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd; and
* retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland, Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.

Coles also has a property development arm, Coles Group Property Developments Ltd (**CGPD**), that buys land and constructs shopping centres, standalone supermarkets and/or liquor outlets and then sells these completed sites to third party buyers.

Neubau Holdings No 22 (the **Vendor**) is an Australian private property development and construction company. The Vendor is based on the Sunshine Coast in Queensland. It specialises in mixed-use, retail, commercial medical, industrial and residential developments.

CGPD has entered into an offer to purchase 22 Palmwoods Montville Road, Palmwoods QLD 4555 (**Target Site**) to facilitate the development of a new standalone Coles supermarket.

Palmwoods is located on the Sunshine Coast, 13km west of Maroochydore and 85km north of Brisbane.

determination_table_content.details:
Coles Group Property Developments Ltd (CGPD), a property
development arm of Coles Group Limited (Coles), applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of a parcel
of land at 22 Palmwoods Montville Road, Palmwoods QLD 4555
(Target Site) from Neubau Holdings No 22 Pty Ltd, as described in
the transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

Coles is an Australian public company (ASX:COL) that primarily
operates:
• supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles
Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd
• retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland,
Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.
The acquirer, CGPD, buys land and constructs shopping centres,
standalone supermarkets and / or liquor outlets and then sells these
completed sites to third party buyers.
The Vendor of the Target Site, Neubau Holdings No 22 Pty Ltd, is an
Australian private property development and construction company,
based on the Sunshine Coast in Queensland. It specialises in mixed-
use, retail, commercial medical, industrial and residential
developments.
The Target Site is located in Palmwoods on the Sunshine Coast,
Queensland. It is the proposed site of a new standalone Coles
supermarket.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. Coles proposes to open a new supermarket site in
Palmwoods, Queensland. Coles does not currently operate
within Palmwoods. The closest existing Coles supermarket
is located more than 6km away from the Target Site
b. there are several alternative grocery retailers in and around
the surrounding local area, including Woolworths, Aldi, IGA,
and Foodworks
c. the Target Site is not currently used for grocery retailing.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds determined under section 51ABP(1) being met. The ACCC
observes that the targeted notification requirements for
supermarkets determined under section 51ABQ(1) may also apply,
but it does not consider it necessary to reach a concluded view in
this regard.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
